title: The Syntax of First-Order Logic
subtopics: Signature: predicate symbols, function symbols, constant symbols
FOL alphabet: variables, predicate symbols, function symbols, connectives, quantifiers
Bound and free occurrences of variables
Modelling English and arithmetic sentences in FOL

definitions.definition: A pair (P, F) where P is a set of predicate symbols (each with an arity) and F is a set of function symbols (each with an arity).

A structure S for signature Σ = (P, F) consists of a non-empty domain D, an interpretation of each predicate symbol as a relation on D, and an interpretation of each function symbol as a function on D.
Inductively: a variable, a constant, or f(t₁, …, tₙ) where f is an n-ary function symbol and t₁, …, tₙ are terms.
A formula of the form P(t₁, …, tₙ) where P is an n-ary predicate symbol and t₁, …, tₙ are terms.
Inductively: an atomic formula, ⊥, ¬φ, φ ∧ ψ, φ ∨ ψ, φ → ψ, φ ↔ ψ, ∀x.φ, or ∃x.φ.
A variable x that occurs free (not bound by any quantifier) in a formula.
A variable x that occurs within the scope of a quantifier ∀x or ∃x.
A formula with no free variables, i.e., free(φ) = ∅.

examples: Modelling 'Any human is mortal' as ∀x.(Human(x) → Mortal(x))
learning_objectives: Explain the motivation for extending propositional logic to FOL.
Define signatures, structures, terms, and FOL formulae.
Identify free and bound variable occurrences.
Model natural language and arithmetic statements in FOL.
